species.real: Jenny has cousins across England, such as Peg Powler of the River Tees, all very handy for keeping children away from deep water.
species.name: Weedjen

dex.text: Lies still under a green carpet of duckweed with only its eyes showing, and giggles when a ball rolls too near the water. The ball is never seen again.
dex.fact: Jenny Greenteeth is a river hag from Lancashire folklore, said to hide under the duckweed and pull in children who strayed too close to the water. Parents told the tale to keep little ones away from ponds that looked like solid grass.

species.real: In warm weather duckweed can double its cover in a couple of days, and scientists are studying it as a fast-growing, protein-rich crop.
species.name: Greenteeth

dex.text: Long green hair, longer green fingers and a grin full of green teeth. Mothers along the Ribble still say her name when a child leans over the bank, and it still works.
dex.fact: Duckweed is one of the smallest flowering plants in the world. It floats in a mat that can cover a still pond completely, which is why the water beneath can look like a lawn you could walk on.
